symptom: arm_wiring has no wiring profile for role acceptor, so the acceptor seat ran its whole pass with no wake plane (no Monitor, no cron; ask_above answers would never wake it).
expected: /acceptor skill boot step 1 instructs: arm_wiring() then run returned monitor_cmd under Monitor and CronCreate verbatim.
evidence: arm_wiring: no wiring profile for role 'acceptor' — known roles: ['curiosity', 'neuron', 'planner', 'reviewer', 'specialist', 'worker']. (code=tool_precondition, retryable=false)
workaround: proceeded unarmed; relied on task-notification wakes + ScheduleWakeup fallback heartbeats for background bench runs
cost: ~5min, no loss this pass (never needed ask_above)

symptom: Sol/codex bridge exit 1 was reported by the s1 planner as a quota cap, but the user's GPT usage is at 54% so it is not a cap; the real codex error was never surfaced. Separately, the .sol_review_err-r*.txt review-path logs are written empty so stderr from the failing call is lost.
expected: A non-zero codex exit should surface the ACTUAL error line (auth/model-id/network/host-spawn), not a hard-coded quota-cap gloss; the review wrapper should capture the stderr that run_sol already merges into .sol-run-*.jsonl.
evidence: sol_bridge.py:546-550 error='codex exited {exit_code}. Treat as a first-class blocker (the CLI exposes no rate-limit telemetry, so a quota cap is only visible on failure)'; empty files .sol_review_err-r12.txt/.sol_review_err-r13.txt/.sol_review_err-r14.txt at repo root
workaround: launched a diagnostic agent to root-cause exit 1 from the raw .sol-run-*.jsonl instead of trusting the quota-cap gloss; endorsed a challenge_waiver for the low-risk s1 step if Sol stays down

symptom: No non-destructive path to set/patch a single action sketch coverage after authoring; add_action silently accepted a sketch_covered_by dict (wrong param, real field is sketch_covers) with no effect, and post-hoc there is no atomic fix.
expected: A per-action patch (update_object action) or idempotent re-declare to set sketch coverage, matching how spec_ids/verify are patchable.
evidence: update_object(action) -> "action field-update allows [...]; got extra [sketch_covers]"; add_action dup -> "already in plan"; update_object(plan) -> "update not supported for plan"; record_plan partial -> "ADD required: plan_id;recipe_id;...;state" then "ADD required actions.N.executor_mode; DROP extra actions.N.sketch_covers". Full record_plan races live workers (c_scaffold went done mid-write, would revert to pending).
workaround: Deferred the sketch-map fix to pre-close quiescence via a full record_plan when no worker is live; recorded a note.

symptom: Action description_ref context files were never written to disk; a_role_inventory and b1_archetype_spec both reported context/action-<id>-<hash>.md missing and recovered from the grounding brief instead.
expected: The description_ref path emitted on the action object should point to a file that exists so workers can load the full brief.
evidence: action a_role_inventory description_ref=context/action-a_role_inventory-7308e02388.md and b1 description_ref=context/action-b1_archetype_spec-c93860a7ad.md; worker flowback: description_ref does not exist on disk, brief recovered from read_object.
workaround: Workers proceeded on the grounding brief (record_grounding_brief injection); no work lost.

symptom: Post-authoring acceptance_sketch remap has no working incremental setter: add_action(sketch_covered_by=...) returns ok but never persists (flowdown advisory still lists every line unmapped), update_object(action, sketch_covers) is refused, record_plan(sketch_covered_by) demands the full plan spec.
expected: One of: update_object(action) accepts sketch_covers, add_action persists sketch_covered_by, or record_plan accepts an incremental sketch_covered_by map without the whole plan.
evidence: update_object refusal: "action field-update allows [...]; got extra [sketch_covers]"; record_plan refusal: "1 validation error ... plan Field required"; add_action returned ok:true with sketch_covered_by dict yet pool_spawn_worker flowdown_gaps still lists all 6 lines unmapped.
workaround: deferred sketch mapping to a full record_plan replan at step-close when actions are terminal (safer than mid-flight)

symptom: User reports they are not actively engaged during the build: after signoff the neuron went heads-down through a long multi-stage s2 with only terse 'OK' status wakes, so the user had no touchpoint to catch that the skeleton looked awful until they proactively asked. The 'speak only at gates' cadence starves the human on long steps.
expected: Neuron guidance says speak to the user at gates; but a long build with no intermediate visual checkpoint leaves an engaged user out of the loop. There should be a proactive intermediate visual/progress surface (e.g. push first-render previews) not just gate-boundary speech.
evidence: neuron output-style 'Speak to the user ONLY at gates'; s2 ran ~40min across skeleton+pendulous+needle stages with no user-facing visual until user asked 'how can I see this?'
workaround: sent grey renders via SendUserFile once the user asked; adding a Sol visual-critique gate
cost: user trust; user had to prompt for visibility

symptom: A user directive from the goal ('use GPT Sol as advisor at any layer / while working') was DROPPED when the conifer specialist authored its doc — the compiled spec had zero mention of sol/advisor/consult, so workers never brought Sol in as visual critic. User concerns are not being carried forward from the verbatim goal into the specialist/worker layer.
expected: Explicit user instructions in the recipe goal should propagate into the specialist docs and worker briefs; the specialist self-scoped it out without flagging the omission.
evidence: grep of .specs/spec-procedural-conifer-geometry/compiled.md for 'sol|advisor|consult|gpt|bridge' returned nothing; goal text: 'You can call GPT Sol at any time at any layer'
workaround: recorded a load-bearing decision + refreshed the specialist to add the Sol-visual-advisor loop
cost: a full geometry stage validated without the mandated visual advisor

symptom: Spawned shells make design/quality decisions autonomously when they are wrong, instead of escalating: the specialist silently narrowed scope (dropped Sol-advisor), and s2 workers/reviewer accepted a visually poor skeleton because numeric conformance gates passed. The seat law forbids shells prompting the user, so a wrong design/look call self-accepts rather than asking up.
expected: When a shell makes a design-level or subjective-quality call that could be wrong (e.g. 'is this skeleton acceptable', 'is dropping an instruction OK'), it should escalate to the neuron/user, not self-accept on a passing numeric gate.
evidence: seat law 'never prompt the user ... never render a choice menu'; r_pendulous verdict '4/4 pass' on a skeleton the user judged 'awful'; specialist scope_covered_and_why self-justified dropping other asset types + the advisor
workaround: neuron now mandates a Sol visual critique + human look-signoff before baseline lock; steering s2
cost: an ugly baseline nearly locked on green gates
